title: Square-zero extensions of sheaves of algebras and additive cotangent Ext
statement:
Let $T$ be a topological space and $R\to A$ a map of sheaves of commutative unital rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the standard polynomial sheaf cotangent complex $L_{A/R}$ [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison], and their derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $G$ be an $A$-module sheaf, placed in degree zero. An extension is an exact sequence $0\to G\xrightarrow{i}E\xrightarrow{p}A\to0$ of additive sheaves, where $E$ is a sheaf of commutative unital $R$-algebras, $p$ is an $R$-algebra map, and its kernel is square zero with the prescribed quotient action on $G$; extension isomorphisms induce the identity on $G$ and $A$. Their isomorphism classes have a canonical bijection $\mathrm{cl}$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(L_{A/R},G[1])$. The split extension $A\oplus G$, with multiplication $(a,g)(b,h)=(ab,ah+bg)$, maps to zero. Pushout along an $A$-linear coefficient map $G\to H$ corresponds to postcomposition on Ext, and the Baer sum, formed by $E_1\times_A E_2$ followed by pushout of the kernel $G\oplus G$ along addition, corresponds to addition in Ext. The bijection commutes with restriction to every open subspace of $T$. For every extension there is a canonical additive identification
$$\operatorname{Aut}_{R,G,A}(E)\cong\operatorname{Der}_{R}(A,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(L_{A/R},G[0]).$$
It sends $d$ to $e\mapsto e+i(d(p(e)))$; composition corresponds to addition. A derivation of sheaves means an additive map obeying the Leibniz rule on local sections and vanishing on $R$. These automorphism identifications commute with open restriction and coefficient pushout. No quasi-coherence, flatness, finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0GPZ (lemma-extensions-of-relative-ringed-spaces), 0GQ0 (remark-extensions-of-relative-ringed-spaces), 0GQ1 (lemma-extensions-of-relative-ringed-spaces-functorial), 0GQ2 (remark-extensions-of-relative-ringed-spaces-functorial), and 08U8 (lemma-huge-diagram-ringed-spaces); full cotangent comparison: cotangent.tex Tags 08US (lemma-compare-cotangent-complex-with-naive) and 08UR (lemma-H0-L-morphism-sheaves-rings).

proof.text: Work on the site of opens of $T$, in a universe containing its opens and all module values. Write $N=\mathrm{NL}_{A/R}$ using the polynomial comparison node, and $K_V=[M_V\xrightarrow{d_V}F_V]$ for a surjective presentation $R[V]\to A$, with comparison $\lambda_V:K_V\simeq N$. On each open $U$ let $K_U$ be the standard ring complex of $A(U)$ over $R(U)$, $P_U=R(U)[A(U)]$, $I_U=\ker(P_U\to A(U))$. The chain projection node gives a chain map $c_U:K_U\to[I_U/I_U^2\to\Omega_{P_U/R(U)}\otimes A(U)]$, identity in degree $0$ and $\rho$ in degree $-1$, commuting strictly with the semilinear maps of the restriction squares $R(U)\to R(W)$, $A(U)\to A(W)$; so the $c_U$ form a map of presheaf complexes. Since $\rho\partial_2=0$, the boundary-cokernel node shows $\rho$ induces $\operatorname{coker}\partial_2\simeq I_U/I_U^2$; thus $c_U$ induces a chain isomorphism $\tau_{\geq-1}K_U\simeq[I_U/I_U^2\to\cdots]$. Sheafify. The full complex becomes $L$ by the sectionwise comparison node. Exact module sheafification preserves kernels and cokernels, hence good truncation. The kernel $J$ of $R[A]\to A$ is the sheafified $I_U$ (underlying sets, finite limits); the sheafified $I_U^2$ is $J^2$, since locally both are finite sums of products; so the term is $J/J^2$. The tensor and differential sheafification nodes identify degree $0$ and its differential with those of $N$. Hence $c:L\to N$ is a chain map inducing a chain isomorphism $\tau_{\geq-1}L\simeq N$, compatible with open restriction because it is sectionwise.

source.place: Tag 08US (lemma-compare-cotangent-complex-with-naive), including its sectionwise sheafification proof; ring input Tag 08RB.

proof.text: For $j=0,1$, precomposition with $c$ is a natural additive isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}(N,G[j])\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(L,G[j])$. To check this, use the standard truncation triangle $C\to L\xrightarrow c N\to C[1]$, where $C\in D^{\leq-2}$. Since $C[1]\in D^{\leq-3}$ and $G[j]\in D^{\geq-j}$, orthogonality makes both $\operatorname{Hom}(C,G[j])$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(C[1],G[j])$ zero. Exactness of Hom applied to this triangle and its rotations gives the isomorphism. Its coefficient naturality is associativity of composition. In what follows first construct classes in $\operatorname{Hom}(N,G[1])$ and then precompose with $c$.

source.place: Tag 08US, passage from naive to full cotangent Ext by the standard truncation triangle.

proof.text: Given an extension $E\twoheadrightarrow A$, take $V$ its underlying sheaf of sets. Evaluation of polynomials and the universal property of sheafification give $a:R[V]\to E$, sending $[e]$ to $e$. It kills $J_V^2$ on $J_V$ and hence induces an $A$-linear map $\delta_a:M_V\to G$. Set $\xi(E)=\partial_V(\delta_a)\lambda_V^{-1}$, using the additive boundary of the two-term node. Any sheaf of generators over $A$ lifting to $E$ can be used. For two choices, their coproduct sheaf has a combined lift; the maps from the two generator sheaves to that coproduct induce the canonical presentation quasi-isomorphisms. Naturality of $\partial$ under the resulting squares of differentials and naturality of $\lambda$ show that both classes equal the class from the coproduct. An isomorphism of extensions preserves the conormal map after composing the lift. Thus $\xi$ is independent of choices and defined on isomorphism classes.

Suppose $E_1,E_2$ have equal classes. Take $V=E_1\times_AE_2$ with polynomial maps $a:R[V]\to E_1$, $b:R[V]\to E_2$, and conormal maps $\delta_1,\delta_2$. Local surjectivity of both extension projections shows that both maps from $V$ to $E_i$, and thus $a,b$, are locally surjective. Boundary exactness gives $\delta_2-\delta_1=\theta d_V$ for an $A$-linear $\theta:F_V\to G$. By the universal property of differentials, $D=\theta(\mathrm d\otimes1):R[V]\to G$ is an $R$-derivation for the action through $A$. Put $b'=b-i_2D$. Expanding products and using the square-zero kernel proves $b'(xy)=b'(x)b'(y)$; it also preserves addition, unit and $R$. On $j\in J_V$ it is $i_2\delta_1(\bar j)$. Therefore if $a(p)=0$, then $p\in J_V$ and $\delta_1(\bar p)=0$, so $b'(p)=0$. Local lifts through $a$ give a unique sheaf algebra map $h:E_1\to E_2$ inducing the identity on $A$ and $G$. Its kernel is zero, since an element there first has zero quotient and then is a kernel element fixed by $h$. Any section of $E_2$ locally lifts its quotient to $E_1$, and its discrepancy from the image is corrected by a section of $G$. Thus $h$ is locally surjective and is an extension isomorphism. This proves injectivity.

source.place: Tag 08U8 (lemma-huge-diagram-ringed-spaces), proof specialized to the identity space map and unchanged base; the equal-class derivation correction.

proof.text: For $\xi\in\operatorname{Hom}(N,G[1])$, the representative node supplies $V$ and $\delta:J_V/J_V^2\to G$ representing $\xi$. Set $Q=R[V]/J_V^2$, $M=J_V/J_V^2\subseteq Q$ and form the sheaf ring $Q\ltimes G$, with $(q,g)(q',g')=(qq',\bar qg'+\bar q'g)$. Quotient by the image of $M\to Q\ltimes G$, $m\mapsto(m,-\delta(m))$. It is an ideal: multiplying by $(q,g)$ gives $(qm,-\bar q\delta(m))=(qm,-\delta(qm))$. In the quotient $E_\delta$, the inclusion $g\mapsto[(0,g)]$ is injective because a graph element with first component zero has $m=0$. The map to $A$ is locally surjective. A local kernel representative $(m,g)$ equals $(0,g+\delta(m))$ in the quotient. Thus the kernel is exactly $G$ and square zero, with the prescribed action. These local kernel statements hold for sheaf quotients by exact sheafification. The polynomial lift $p\mapsto[(p,0)]$ sends $j$ to $i(\delta(\bar j))$, so its class is $\xi$. This proves surjectivity, and Steps 2--4 give the required canonical bijection for the full $L$.

source.place: Tag 0GQ0 and the pushout construction in Tag 08UC (lemma-choices-ringed-spaces); representative input Tag 08UJ on the site of opens.

proof.text: For $A\oplus G$ choose generator sheaf $A$ with lift $a\mapsto(a,0)$; its polynomial lift kills the presentation ideal, so its conormal map and class are zero. For $u:G\to H$, form the coefficient pushout as $(E\ltimes H)/\{(i(g),-u(g))\}$, where $E$ acts through $A$. Its graph is an ideal by $A$-linearity. The local kernel calculation of Step 5 gives an extension by $H$, and the induced polynomial lift has conormal map $u\delta$. Naturality of the boundary under postcomposition gives $\xi(u_*E)=u_*\xi(E)$, hence the same formula for $\mathrm{cl}$. This does not require $u$ to be injective or surjective.

source.place: Tags 0GPZ and 0GQ2 (remark-extensions-of-relative-ringed-spaces-functorial); split origin and explicit coefficient pushout.

proof.text: For two extensions by $G$, use $V=E_1\times_AE_2$. Its polynomial lift to this fibre product has conormal map $(\delta_1,\delta_2)$ with values in $G\oplus G$. Coefficient pushout along addition replaces this by $\delta_1+\delta_2$. Additivity of $\partial_V$ gives $\xi(E_1+E_2)=\xi(E_1)+\xi(E_2)$, and precomposition with $c$ preserves addition. This is the Baer sum in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0GQ0 explicit representative; the fibre-product-then-addition calculation of Baer sum.

proof.text: Let $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be open. Restriction is the inverse image of module sheaves, which is additive and preserves finite limits and colimits; it therefore acts termwise on derived categories and preserves the triangle defining $\partial_V$. Polynomial sheaf formation, kernels, ideal squares, quotients, and differentials restrict to their counterparts on $U$: for an open $W\subseteq U$ their local formulas and their covering families are exactly those on $T$. Sheafification on $U$ agrees with restriction of sheafification on $T$, because sections of a sheafification are locally represented and glued over the same coverings of $W$. The structure map $\alpha:V\to A$ is a map of presentations over $A$, so the naturality and identity clauses of the polynomial comparison node give $\lambda_V=\lambda_A K(\alpha)=K(\alpha)$, a chain map whose formulas restrict; $c$ restricts by Step 1. Restricting a polynomial lift therefore gives precisely $\delta_a|_U$, and restricting $\partial_V(\delta_a)\lambda_V^{-1}c$ gives the class of $E|_U$. This proves compatibility of the bijection with every open restriction, including the empty open.

source.place: Tags 0GQ0 and 0GQ2, restricted to open subspaces; cotangent.tex Tag 08US, sectionwise comparison.

proof.text: For an $R$-derivation $d:A\to G$, define $T_d(e)=e+i(d(p(e)))$. Expanding a product gives the cross term $i(p(e)d(p(e'))+p(e')d(p(e)))=i(d(p(ee')))$; the product of two kernel terms is zero. Hence $T_d$ is an $R$-algebra map fixing kernel and quotient, with inverse $T_{-d}$. Conversely for an automorphism $T$ fixing both ends, $T-\mathrm{id}$ takes values in $i(G)$ and vanishes on $i(G)$. Local lifts through $p$ therefore define a unique additive sheaf map $d:A\to G$. Independence of lifts follows from vanishing on the kernel; multiplicativity gives Leibniz, and fixing $R$ gives vanishing on $R$. Thus $T=T_d$ uniquely. Finally $T_dT_e=T_{d+e}$, since $pT_e=p$. This proves the canonical additive identification with derivations.

The universal property of sheaf differentials gives $\operatorname{Der}_R(A,G)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(\Omega_{A/R},G)$. The polynomial comparison identifies $\Omega_{A/R}$ with $\operatorname{coker}d_V$, so the degree-zero assertion of the two-term boundary node identifies this group with $\operatorname{Hom}(N,G[0])$. Precompose with $c$ using Step 2 to obtain $\operatorname{Hom}(L,G[0])$. These are additive identifications: the universal derivation correspondence is linear in its target, the two-term node is additive, and composition in the derived category is additive.

Under restriction the formula for $T_d$ becomes the identical formula for $d|_U$, and the differential universal map, the two-term boundary and $c$ restrict as in Steps 1 and 8. For coefficient pushout $q:E\to u_*E$, one has $qi_G=i_Hu$, hence $qT_d(e)=q(e)+i_Hu(d(p(e)))=T_{ud}q(e)$. On the added $H$ summand the induced automorphism is the identity, so this equality identifies it on every local representative in the pushout quotient. The universal derivation identification and the degree-zero two-term identification are natural under postcomposition; precomposition with $c$ preserves that equality. Thus both automorphism identifications have all the required naturalities. Every calculation used only local lifts and square-zero multiplication, with arbitrary module sheaves.
